summary: Phase 1 of the cinematic gameplay video (docs/video/PLAN.md), after Gate 1: the world's round 2 (drawn detail, no glare, Game-boy's direction), the upgraded cast, the cine stage
read_first: docs/video/PLAN.md §2 (the style bible), §4 (Plan A) and §6's Gate 2 rubric
docs/video/P1.md, 'What Phase 0 found' and 'Shared by all four packages'
note: VIDEO WORK OVERRIDES: cine (non-first-person) shots count as much as first person. Judge against docs/video/PLAN.md §2 and the reference frames, not SPEC.md. Never edit game/, tuning/ or tests/: look values go in CineLook .tres files under video/look/, not in tuning_data.gd. Instead of the full suite, run the video tests (PLAN.md §6, LD-RENDER) and `git diff --quiet origin/video/cinematic-trailer -- game tuning tests` (it must exit 0). Calls files go to docs/video/calls/<key>.md. PHASE 1: your brief is your section of docs/video/P1.md (in P1.md, 'CineLook' is split into VideoLookPiece resources by owner). In the structured result, tests_passed and tests_total are the video tests (video/tests), not the main suite, and feel_judgement holds your honest pillar scores (PLAN.md §6 rubric) for what you built, judged at full resolution beside the reference frames and the Gemini targets. Python only through ~/.venvs/beat-em-up-video/bin/python -I (never pip install). The reference frames and targets are untracked files in other worktrees: read them, never copy them into git. This is an 8 GB machine with Game-boy's own Blender open: one Godot process at a time from you, always with --quit-after, and the capture lock for every windowed run.
